name: keyring_daemon_limits

storage.rationale: The safeguard writes one systemd user drop-in inside the invoking user's home and restarts a user unit; it needs no privilege and creates no host-wide state.

description: Raise gnome-keyring-daemon's file-descriptor limit through a systemd user drop-in and restart the daemon when it nears the limit, so a client leak cannot wedge secret access, console login, and the system log

linux.reason: Host safeguards mutate host state and cannot ship in a desktop bundle.

macos.reason: Host safeguards mutate host state and cannot ship in a desktop bundle.

windows.reason: Host safeguards mutate host state and cannot ship in a desktop bundle.

macos.evidence: macOS keeps credentials in Keychain Services, which has no per-daemon descriptor limit failure mode.

windows.evidence: Windows keeps credentials in Credential Manager / DPAPI, which has no per-daemon descriptor limit failure mode.
